scope: Full read-only review of SMO001–012 and B01–06 against French physical pages 93–94 and English physical page 61.
mathematical_checks: The original smooth projection q cannot be the unramified map when N−m>0; the point-line incidence counterexample meets all initial and bad-parameter axioms.
The fiber map q_xi is unramified at z iff the incidence map j is unramified there, via base change for relative differentials and Nakayama.
The three good fiber conditions are simultaneous; their failure is not simultaneous failure of all three.
For fixed x,V, flattening strata and the rank condition on V-perp to relative differentials give constructibility; the dimension inequality remains an independent axiom.
The Frobenius example correctly separates regularity of a field from smoothness over its ground field.
In the smooth-P and smooth-X part, mathcal P and mathcal X are smooth over k and therefore reduced. Their maps factor through G_red and the displayed base change identifications are valid.
The nonreduced-parameter counterexample satisfies the fiberwise bad-parameter axiom yet fails flatness everywhere; generic flatness over G_red gives a common nonempty open U for the two families.

On U, tangent transversality gives smooth fiber products. Quasi-finiteness bounds bad-point fibers by bad-parameter images, and the componentwise generic fiber dimension argument supplies the uniform bound dim E≤N−1.
The local-property regularity condition established in the front half is not replaced by the later smoothness conclusion.
French 2.12–2.18, 7.3 without prime, and the negation and (c) in both 8.7(c) mentions were checked in actual page images.

flatness plus smooth fiber is the precise relative smoothness criterion in B04/B05
generic fiber dimension is constant on a nonempty open; supports B05 counting

decision: Pass; no additional source or mathematical correction requested.
not_claimed: No independent proof of every historical analogue 2.12–2.18 or 4/5/7. No recovery of the unfinished object after Il faut une condition sur. No final integrated rendering approval.
